question.text: A nucleus of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>M</mi></math> at rest splits into two parts having masses <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>'</mo></msup><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>'</mo></msup></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mfenced><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>'</mo></msup><mo><</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>. The ratio of de Broglie wavelength of two parts will be

solution.text:
Since the initial momentum of the system is zero. To keep the final momentum zero, the momentum of both parts should be equal and opposite in direction.

P→1=P→2

Here P→ is momentum

De-Broglie wavelength is given by λ=hP

Hence, both will have same de Broglie wavelength.

Therefore, λ1:λ2=1:1.
